learner_entry_state.credit_rule: Only prior concepts marked USABLE count as learned.
learner_entry_state.critical_dependency_warning: S16 is AUDITED_REPAIR_REQUIRED. Its clean/quarantine partition, PEN/category normalization, schema enforcement and audit provenance are not safe prerequisites. S15 DataFrame.join/concat mental models also remain unsafe.
not_creditable: S16 output is clean merely because it is named clean
schema set check as complete schema gate

roadmap_expectation.T1: joins with cardinality/fan-out validation and anti-join evidence
roadmap_expectation.T2: concat and long/wide reshape with stable output schema
roadmap_expectation.T3: groupby/agg/transform plus ordered windows and cohorts
roadmap_expectation.T4: reconciled totals/denominators and temporal cutoff/as-of controls
roadmap_expectation.gate: reproducible analytical close whose row universe, totals, denominators, exclusions and time boundary are explainable

live_site.card_tagline: Portfolio ejecutivo de calidad + EDA: dataset limpio, script reproducible, reconciliación y preguntas de negocio
live_site.note: The public crawl exposes the S17 card, but not the hash-routed lesson theory. Detailed source-to-render parity remains unproven.

adversarial_review.most_likely_beginner_failure: Treat row growth, orphan coverage, client counts and reconciliation as separate checks and therefore accept a plausible dashboard that contains null-key false matches, unseen right-side orphans or transaction-row counts mislabeled as client counts.
adversarial_review.suspected_hidden_prerequisite: A fully validated S16 clean dataset plus safe pandas Index/concat semantics from S15; neither is creditable in the effective ledger.
adversarial_review.most_likely_misconception: If totals still sum and validate did not raise, the join/reshape/aggregation must have preserved the intended business grain.
three_adversarial_questions: Can the learner prove every row in an S17 aggregate belongs to the declared universe, including missing join/group keys and right-side orphans?
Can the learner distinguish preserved total from preserved grain after pivot_table, concat and groupby?
Can the final reconciliation actually fail when an upstream join is wrong, or is it separately hand-authored arithmetic?

confirmed_findings.evidence: S17 assumes a clean dataset and clean keys from S16, while effective S16 leaves clean/quarantine partitioning, money/category normalization, schema enforcement and provenance non-USABLE.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can carry duplicated/quarantined rows or invalid canonical keys into joins and treat the aggregates as analysis-ready.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Every later S17 control assumes the analytical universe is valid.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add an S17 entry preflight proving disjoint clean/quarantine, non-null normalized join keys and required schema before merge.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Callout says str-int join produces false orphans; current pandas commonly rejects string/object versus integer merge keys with ValueError before an orphan table exists.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can diagnose the wrong failure surface or assume a successful merge proves semantic alignment.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Say incompatible dtypes may raise; compatible text can still mismatch semantically. Normalize and validate representation plus values.

confirmed_findings.evidence: No null-key policy exists. pandas matches null merge keys to null keys. A one-null left key can be is_unique and pass one_to_many; is_unique and nunique()==len disagree because nunique drops missing by default.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Missing cliente_id can match missing transaction ids and manufacture false relationships while validate passes.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: False matches manufacture evidence rather than merely losing coverage.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Reject/quarantine null join keys before merge; explain pandas null-match behavior and use one uniqueness check after missing policy.

confirmed_findings.evidence: `merge` and `join` are grouped as interchangeable key joins. DataFrame.join is index-oriented by default and join(on=key) matches the caller column to the other frame Index; S15 already left this unsafe.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can join on the wrong right-hand key/index and obtain plausible misalignment.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Teach merge(on=...) as primary column-key operation; separately microdefine DataFrame.join index semantics with set_index.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The normal client-to-transactions 1:m merge omits validate; the only theory validate call deliberately fails one_to_one.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can treat validate as an after-the-fact debugging stunt instead of a routine executable contract.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use validate='one_to_many' on the canonical successful join, then contrast with a failing contract.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Text promises C002 left orphan and C003 right orphan, but code uses how='left'; that result cannot contain right_only and only prints C002.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can inspect a left merge for right_only, see none and incorrectly conclude no orphan transactions exist.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Transaction-without-master rows are a referential-integrity problem.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use outer+indicator or two explicit bilateral anti joins and print both sides with denominators.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Callout says 'anti-join de duplicados' although the lesson elsewhere correctly defines anti-join as unmatched rows and fan-out/duplicates as a different failure.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can try to detect duplicate-key fan-out with left_only/right_only instead of uniqueness/cardinality checks.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Say 'exporta las claves duplicadas y, por separado, los anti-joins de filas sin pareja'.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Concat is an explicit outcome but has no theory worked example. One sentence omits alignment on the non-concatenation axis and default outer label behavior; S15 concat semantics were already unsafe.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can be surprised by inserted missing values, duplicate columns or index alignment that does not follow physical row position.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add axis=0 and axis=1 worked examples with mismatched labels, including join/ignore_index/keys.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Figure/prose frame wide and long as the same data and send melt output 'de regreso' through pivot_table. pivot_table aggregates duplicate index/column combinations and can destroy row-level detail; pivot instead requires uniqueness.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can believe melt→pivot_table(sum) is an information-preserving inverse because the total still matches.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Preserved totals do not prove preserved grain.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Teach pivot as reshape with unique pairs and pivot_table as reshape-plus-aggregation; add a duplicate-pair counterexample.

confirmed_findings.evidence: `len(long)==n_clientes*n_meses` only holds if each wide row is one unique client and all selected value columns are months; general melt count is source rows × value_vars.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Duplicate client rows can make the formula encode a false grain assumption.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use len(wide)*len(value_vars), then separately assert unique client grain when intended.

confirmed_findings.evidence: set(df.columns)==set(expected) discards multiplicity. Duplicate column labels can pass membership even though names are ambiguous.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can pass the declared schema gate with duplicate columns and later select/export ambiguous data.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Check columns.is_unique, then missing/extra sets, and order separately when required.

confirmed_findings.evidence: No missing-group policy is declared. pandas GroupBy defaults dropna=True, so rows with missing region can contribute to raw totals yet disappear from regional parts without an exception.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can publish segmented totals that silently omit unclassified rows and misread the residual as unexplained loss.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: This violates the section's universe/denominator/reconciliation promise.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Explicitly quarantine, bucket or group missing keys with dropna=False and reconcile included/excluded rows.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Prose discusses client counts, but code has no cliente_id and defines n=('monto','size'), which counts rows/transactions, not unique clients.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can use transaction rows as a client denominator and produce misleading rates/averages.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Denominator correctness is a stated section outcome.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add cliente_id and publish n_rows=size separately from n_clientes=nunique.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Text says resample requires DatetimeIndex. DataFrame.resample also supports a datetime-like column with on= or a datetime-like MultiIndex level with level=.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can unnecessarily mutate the index or conclude resample is unavailable with a normal datetime column.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Say resample needs a datetime-like index/level, or a DataFrame datetime column supplied via on=.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Prose mixes 'periodos' and '7d' while code uses rolling(3), which means three observations. Default rolling includes the current observation; prior-only/as-of rolling is not contrasted.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can call rolling(7) a seven-day measure on irregular data or use current-inclusive rolling as if it used only prior history.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Contrast observation windows vs time windows and descriptive current-inclusive vs shift/closed-left prior-only windows.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Amounts are repeatedly labeled PEN but represented as Python floats and reconciled with float eps. S02 established Decimal for soles and S17 introduces no explicit analytical conversion boundary.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can abandon the earlier exact-money contract during aggregation/reconciliation without understanding precision tradeoffs.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Monetary reconciliation is a correctness gate here.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Keep canonical PEN as Decimal, or explicitly teach/preserve a Decimal→analytical-float boundary and its precision policy.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Code hand-authors total=100 and parts 60/30/10 in a fresh object; neither is derived from T1-T3. Therefore the claimed upstream fan-out cannot make this check fail.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can hand-enter matching totals, get ok=True and believe a broken pipeline is reconciled.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Reconciliation is the section-level closure mechanism.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use one shared fixture: source total → validated join → aggregate → explicit exclusions/residual → reconstructed total.

confirmed_findings.evidence: T4-B demonstrates cutoff only with a separate sum; it does not govern transform or rolling introduced immediately before, and default rolling is current-inclusive.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can reproduce the cutoff demo yet still calculate historical transform/rolling features from the full dataset and call the workflow leakage-safe.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Filter/as-of before the earlier aggregation/feature and show prior-only rolling; distinguish post-cutoff data from actual use of future information.

confirmed_findings.evidence: EDA, portfolio, stakeholder and claims appear before Spanish-first definitions; EDA's dedicated mental model is S18. The quick dictionary omits these deliverable-bearing terms.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: ZERO_TECH learner can understand code but not know what 'portfolio ejecutivo + EDA' or a causal claim is supposed to mean.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: First use: análisis exploratorio de datos (EDA), portafolio, parte interesada/destinatario (stakeholder), afirmación causal; keep S18 as deeper EDA.

code_audit.observed: Output is correct for fixture, but no validate and no null-key policy.
code_audit.improved_direction: Reject/quarantine null keys, verify left uniqueness, execute with validate='one_to_many'.

code_audit.observed: Left merge cannot produce right_only; C003 is never emitted.
Unique fixture round-trip works, but no concat example and no duplicate-pivot counterexample.
code_audit.improved_direction: Teach concat and pivot vs pivot_table grain loss.

code_audit.observed: Default groupby drops missing region; n=size counts rows; PEN uses float; transform has no cutoff boundary.
code_audit.improved_direction: Explicit missing policy, n_rows/n_clients, Decimal boundary, as-of filter.

code_audit.observed: Output is correct; rolling count/time and current/prior-only semantics are underexplained; resample requirement is overstated.
code_audit.improved_direction: Contrast observation/time windows and prior-only rolling; fix resample model.

code_audit.observed: Hardcoded arithmetic is disconnected from upstream transformations and cannot catch fan-out.
code_audit.improved_direction: Derive reference and parts from shared fixture.

code_audit.observed: 115 vs 15 is correct, but cutoff is not transferred to transform/rolling.
code_audit.improved_direction: Apply cutoff before a prior feature and show prior-only rolling.

source_only_meta_text.text: Matching content to the slug is how three agent diagrams ended up attached to a data-testing lesson.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: Any join row growth is a defect.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: 1:m joins legitimately grow; the defect is undeclared/contract-violating growth.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: pandas 3 native left_anti/right_anti must replace indicator=True.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: Native anti joins exist, but indicator remains valid and pedagogically transparent.
Sum may be preserved; grain/detail can still be lost.
Missing groups may be excluded by explicit policy; silent default exclusion is the defect.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: size is inherently the wrong aggregation.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: size correctly counts rows; the defect is confusing row count with clients.
It is valid descriptive EDA; prior-only use needs a different boundary.
Float can be appropriate; this course already set a Decimal-for-PEN contract and provides no conversion boundary.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: Detailed live S17 is proven different from source.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: Only card metadata is retrievable; detailed render mismatch is unproven.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: The source header comment is a learner meta-leak.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: It is a TypeScript comment with no render evidence.

technical_spot_checks.result: One left null matched two right nulls under validate=one_to_many; validate passed.
left+indicator cannot emit C003 right_only; outer+indicator can.
raw sum 35; default region groupby accounted 30; dropna=False accounted 35.
two Lima rows from one client give size=2 but unique clients=1.
pivot raises on duplicate id/month; pivot_table(sum) collapses 10+20 to 30.
rolling(3) includes current observation; shifted rolling is prior-only.

USABLE: cohort as first valid observation period

priority_repairs.action: Repair join boundary and bilateral evidence.
Make aggregation/reconciliation preserve a declared universe and derive close from one fixture.
Repair time semantics and apply cutoff to feature operations.
Restore or explicitly bridge Decimal-for-PEN contract.
Correct diagnostic terminology and widow terms.

rules: Do not inherit groupby/agg/transform as fully USABLE: missing-key universe and client-vs-row denominator remain PARTIAL.
Do not inherit monetary totals as trustworthy until Decimal/analytical boundary is explicit.
Do not assume S17 reconciliation proved pipeline conservation; T4-A is hardcoded and disconnected.
Do not treat pivot_table output as grain-preserving merely because sums match.
Do not inherit rolling as prior-only; current-inclusive/default semantics remain PARTIAL.
Do not assume EDA is already taught merely because S17 uses the acronym; S18 owns its full model.
Carry cutoff/as-of basic principle as USABLE but require integration with each time-dependent metric.
S18 rates/averages must distinguish row count from unique-entity denominator and state missing-group policy.
